pull.title: streams: handle buffered write failures outside the destructor
pull.body:
**Problem:** Block and undo writers buffer serialized data, then rely on the `BufferedWriter` destructor to write the remaining bytes.
`fwrite()` can report fewer bytes written than requested after a local storage error, e.g., if the filesystem fills up while a block is being written (my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up, so I've been seeing these failures more often).
`AutoFile::write_buffer()` converts that result into an exception, and because the destructor is implicitly non-throwing, the exception invokes `std::terminate`.
Calling `flush()` before destruction is insufficient on its own because a failed flush leaves the same bytes pending, so the destructor retries the write while the original exception unwinds.

I introduced this bug in #31551 when adding `BufferedWriter`.

**Fix:** Block and undo writers now flush explicitly before destruction, catch write errors, log their cause, and request normal fatal shutdown, consistently with the adjacent file-close error handling.
`BufferedWriter` clears the pending byte count before writing, preventing a destructor retry after a failed flush.
The destructor uses `Assume` to detect missing explicit flushes before attempting a fallback flush.
`flush()` continues to propagate exceptions, and `AutoFile` remains unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Manual write-error reproducer</summary>

Force the error path in `AutoFile::write_buffer()`:

```sh
sed -i '' '/^.*AutoFile::write_buffer(/,/^}/s/!= src.size()/!= 0/' src/streams.cpp
cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j5 && build/bin/bitcoind -regtest -datadir="$(mktemp -d)"; echo "exit=$?"
```

Before this change, implicit flushing invokes `std::terminate`:

> libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::ios_base::failure: AutoFile::write_buffer: write failed: unspecified iostream_category error
> zsh: abort      build/bin/bitcoind -regtest -datadir="$(mktemp -d)"
> exit=134

With this change, `bitcoind` logs the write failure, then completes normal shutdown and exits with status 1:

> Checking all blk files are present...
> [error] Failed to write block file FlatFilePos(nFile=0, nPos=8): AutoFile::write_buffer: write failed: unspecified iostream_category error
> ...
> Error: A fatal internal error occurred, see debug.log for details: Failed to write block.
> [error] Writing genesis block to disk failed
> [error] Error initializing block database
> ...
> Shutdown done
> exit=1
</details>

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

> the exception invokes std::terminate instead of reaching normal storage-error handling.

Can you expand on why this is a problem? If there is a storage error, don't we have to crash anyways?

> If there is a storage error, don't we have to crash anyways?

Yes, the node still has to stop, but `std::terminate` bypasses the existing error handling.

> Can you expand on why this is a problem?

Handling the exception lets the node report the storage error and run its normal shutdown cleanup.

This reminds me of the other "exceptions can terminate" topics.

It would be good to find a code pattern that avoids this class of problem wholesale. It doesn't seem a great use of human (or LLM) review time to spend on such issues one-by-one. If we care about those issues, it would be better if the compiler or a clang-tidy analysis could find and prevent all of them.

Concept ACK

I ran into the same bug while working in this area and implemented an alternative fix before finding this PR.

My version removes writes from the `BufferedWriter` destructor and requires explicit final flushing. It also adjusts `AutoFile` cleanup during exception unwinding and adds an exception handler for undo-write failures.

https://github.com/w0xlt/bitcoin/tree/streams/buffered-write-errors

Feel free to reuse anything you find useful.

Thanks @w0xlt, I used your explicit-flush and undo-write error-handling ideas and credited you as a co-author.

But I think forgetting to call `flush()` is a bigger practical risk than the rare exception from a destructor write, so I kept destructor flushing as a fallback. Block and undo writes now flush explicitly and handle failures, and a failed flush is no longer retried during exception unwinding.
ACK cac9501d355d9853c17dcfa874d85c8e952cece0
LGTM

How is this different from AutoFile? Shouldn't this use the same `    bool m_was_written{false};` approach with flush+Assume+LogErr? Otherwise, we are just spending manual review on this and this will silently break again in the future?

Ok, I see. So the difference is whether the dtor can throw. That is probably an internal implementation detail.

Though, the underlying issue seems to be that we want to notify the caller about a flush failure and that doesn't really work well via a dtor. So the fix for that is an explicit flush. However, if we want those explicit flushes, it should be enforced in the same way as it is done in AutoFile.

I think your suggested diff achieves that, so my preference would be to focus this pull on that. In theory, one could even drop the exception fixup from this pull afterward, and instead make `flush` non-throwing, so that `m_buf_pos=0` can be forced in the dtor, so that a failed flush isn't immediately tried again. (If it failed to flush, re-trying it a single CPU cycle later isn't going to fix it anyway). Up to you, if you want to make `flush` non-throwing and instead use a nodiscard-result, but I think your suggested diff  with the `Assume` would be good regardless.

events.body: Thanks for the hints @maflcko, played with it a bit, now `write_buffer` is `noexcept` with a `bool` return value - and buffered flush failures log their cause and abort. Explicit final flushing is enforced with `Assume`, while destructor flushing remains as a prod fallback. This seems like a more holistic fix than before, let me know what you think.

Ok, I see you now changed `write_buffer` to be nodiscard and `flush` to abort on error. This seems fine, but is now basically the behavior that existed before this pull (it also crashes).

My preference would be to make `flush` nodiscard (and possibly not even touch `write_buffer`/`AutoFile` here). This would be more consistent with the existing AutoFile `fclose` "flush" method.

> basically the behavior that existed before this pull (it also crashes)

We're always flushing explicitly outside the destructor now. It's a small difference, I know, mostly consistency and belts-and-suspenders hardening. These unlikely write/flush/read failure cases are still all over the place...
Reverted the `AutoFile` changes and updated `flush()` to return a checked result.

Restored the try/catch approach from the ACKed 6e17d09, following @maflcko's latest suggestion, and added the destructor’s `Assume(m_buf_pos == 0)` check. This means `flush()` isn't returning anymore (still throwing), with block and undo writers flushing explicitly and handling failures through their normal storage-error paths. It's not perfect, but it's better than before.
(edit: previous push didn't succeed for some reason)
